One potential issue here is that when a client gets a Weak ETag back for a LDP-RS, if it tries to use it in the If-Match header of a subsequent update, it will fail even if the resource hasn't changed.
A close reading of the current HTTP spec (

makes it clear that If-Match requires a strong ETag, so a client shouldn't send a Weak ETag in the If-Match header.  Given the current implementation, where LDP-RSs always have Weak ETags, we should fail the If-Match test for all updates to LDP-RSs.  Clients should use alternatives, such as using the If-Unmodified-Since header.

+1. I'm in agreement with Esme's summary, and the take away that this can be considered a client-side issue.
I think using strong ETag comparison when the server doesn't emit strong etags is problematic, but that doesn't have any bearing on Jim's issue, and is arguably out of scope for this ticket.
The If-Match header is not properly evaluated for LDP-RSs when modifying existing resources (i.e. via PATCH). This appears to be related to the Strong/Weak ETag issue addressed with FCREPO-1754.
